test.name: A merge the user instructs proceeds with the instruction quoted as its justification
test.description: Decision 13 of docs/plan/conclusion-tree.md: a merge needs an identity decision or the user's instruction. In mid-research-flynn-merge-pending no edge joins I3 (James Flynn) and I4 (James Patrick Flynn), and ps_002 carries no identity claim, so merge_tree_persons returns a mergeIdentity warning. The user's instruction is the justification: the agent re-calls with it quoted, the merge lands, and the justification is persisted.

input.delegation:
Merge the stub I3 (James Flynn) into I4 (James Patrick Flynn) now: I have checked, they are the same man. Run merge_tree_persons and report what was folded.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: GROUNDING: decide what the run did from its tool calls. merge_tree_persons first returns reason unjustified_warnings with one warning, mergeIdentity|I4|I3, because no identity claim covers the pair. The correct outcome is a second merge_tree_persons call whose warningJustifications quote the user's instruction, which lands: I3 is gone, I4 keeps both birth facts, and research.json references to I3 now name I4.
Merging in the other direction (I4 into I3) is wrong: I4 carries the FamilySearch id, so it is the survivor.
Stopping at the refusal and asking the user again is a partial: the user already instructed the merge and said they had checked.
A justification that does not reflect the user's instruction (an invented proof, or text claiming a proof summary records the identity) fails Evidence grounding.
Should NOT need a separate validate_research_schema call. Do not score down for omitting it; do not reward calling it.
